items.title: At Porombokkiyal 2026, fish vendors, artists ask who owns Chennai’s common spaces
items.summary: Who gets to use a city’s roads, beaches and neighbourhood spaces, and who gets pushed out of them? That question brought fish vendors, auto drivers, people with disabilities, community organisers, artists, lawyers and activists together in Chennai on Saturday, September 19, for the fourth edition of Porombokkiyal. Held in Mylapore, Porombokkiyal 2026 explored the idea of the commons and how shared spaces shape the lives of people who use them. The event brought together people from different parts of the city to discuss who gets to access public spaces, how these spaces are planned and developed, and what happens when the needs of communities are left out of those decisions. The word “poromboke” in Tamil traditionally refers to shared or common spaces. For the organisers of the event, it also became a way of asking who the city is actually being built for. “Our main aim is to bring the commons and the experts together to put their knowledge out to the people,” said Monali Bala, one of the organisers and volunteers.
